Subject: Demo booked — shows wrong local time in my calendar

Hi Hannah,

We just clicked the Calendly link you sent and it created a calendar event at 08:00 AM my local time (AEST), but the Calendly page showed 08:00 PM. Two of our folks in India and Sydney are seeing different times in their calendar apps.

Attached is a screenshot from Calendly and the invite that landed in Google Calendar — looks like the .ics is missing the VTIMEZONE block or Calendly is defaulting to a timezone on your account. Can we please have someone send a manual invite? Our local team needs the event at 20:00 AEDT / 15:30 IST / 03:00 PST (your UTC conversion showed 09:00 UTC).

Thanks,
Andrew

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Demo booked — shows wrong local time in my calendar

Hi Andrew — sorry about the confusion and thanks for the screenshot. I can confirm we saw a small edge case yesterday where scheduling links created by Calendly/Chili Piper sometimes emit ICS files without the full timezone rule set; some calendar clients then display using the viewer's local DST rules which leads to the apparent AM/PM flip.

Short fixes (pick one):
- I'll ask Camila to send a manual .ics with an explicit VTIMEZONE (works in Google/Outlook/iOS).
- If you prefer auto-booking, try the Calendly link with the tz parameter that forces Australia/Sydney (https://calendly.com/redwood/demo?tz=Australia%2FSydney).
- As a fallback, we can set the meeting time explicitly in your timezone and I will create the invite from my calendar and send.

Camila — can you create a manual invite that pins to Australia/Sydney and include a short agenda? Marcus, can you add a note in our side to prefer the tz param for future APAC bookings?

Andrew — if you confirm which of the three options you prefer, we will action immediately.

— Hannah
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:22:00 +1100
Subject: Re: Demo booked — manual invite attached (apac_manual_invite.ics)

Hi Andrew,

Thanks Hannah — I created and attached a manual invite (apac_manual_invite.ics) that pins the event to Australia/Sydney (AEDT) and includes the VTIMEZONE block so clients import the correct DST offsets. I also attached a short one-page agenda (demo-agenda.pdf).

For transparency, two quick notes we send to customers when this happens:
- If using Calendly/Chili Piper links, append the tz query parameter to force the target timezone (example: ?tz=Asia%2FKolkata or ?tz=Australia%2FSydney).
- If a calendar still shows an incorrect hour, open the .ics in a text editor and verify there is a VTIMEZONE block — if missing, import the attached .ics instead.

Meeting details I put in the invite (local conversions included):
- 2026-11-12 20:00 AEDT (Australia/Sydney)
- 2026-11-12 15:30 IST (Asia/Kolkata)
- 2026-11-12 02:00 PST (US/Pacific) — crossing midnight PT, please confirm if this is OK for your west-coast attendees

Attachment: apac_manual_invite.ics (text/calendar)
Attachment: demo-agenda.pdf (application/pdf)

If that looks good, accept the invite and it should show correct local time in your calendar. Marcus, I'll add a small doc in our internal runbook describing the Calendly tz param and the ICS VTIMEZONE requirement.

— Camila
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
